subject: Chemistry
title: What is Matter?
summary: Anything that has mass and takes up space is matter, even the air you cannot see.
keyPoints: Air is matter: it fills a balloon and has mass.
Light, sound, heat and feelings are **not** matter.
SI unit of mass: kg; of volume: m³ (1 L = 1 dm³ = 1000 mL).

blocks.p: A pencil, water, food, stones, steam and your own body are all **matter**: each has **mass** and occupies **space**. Both conditions must be true.

head: Term
Meaning
SI unit
rows: Anything that has mass and occupies space
The amount of matter in an object
cubic metre (m³); also litre (L), 1 L = 1 dm³ = 1000 mL

blocks.alt: A balloon swelling with air, and a balance tipping towards the full balloon
blocks.caption: Air takes up space and has mass, so air is matter.

list: **Space:** blow air into a balloon. It swells, so air occupies space.
**Mass:** balance a full and an empty balloon on a metre stick. It tips towards the full one, so air has mass.

head: Matter
Not matter
rows: Pencil, water, food, air, our body, stones, steam

blocks.p: **Common mistakes:** only things we can see are matter (air is invisible but is matter); sound is matter (sound travels through matter, it is not matter); mixing up mass and volume (a balloon can have a large volume but a small mass).

quiz.explain: Air has mass and occupies space, so it is matter. Light, sound and feelings are not.

options: Yes, it has mass and occupies space
quiz.explain: Smoke is made of tiny particles; it has mass and occupies space.

options: No, it is only an absence of light
quiz.explain: A shadow has no mass and takes up no space; it is just where light is blocked.

quiz.q: A balanced metre stick tips towards the full balloon. This shows that air:
quiz.explain: The full balloon is heavier, so the air inside it has mass.
